strings.name: María Corina Machado
strings.summary: Trained in industrial engineering, Machado entered public affairs through election-monitoring group Súmate, then served in parliament and led Vente Venezuela. She won the 2023 opposition primary but was barred from the following presidential election. She backed González and challenged official results. Awarded the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, she returned to Venezuela in 2026 while advocating democratic transition.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Long involved in Venezuelan opposition politics and electoral mobilisation, attracting international attention through advocacy for democratic transition and civil rights.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Industrial engineering, Andrés Bello Catholic University; finance studies at IESA.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Electoral mobilisation
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from civic monitoring to opposition organisation and presidential primaries.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Nobel Peace Prize
strings.highlights.h2.text: Honoured in 2025 for democratic rights and peaceful transition in Venezuela.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Returned to Venezuela
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Nobel Committee welcomed her return and urged peaceful democratic transition.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t2.text: The committee recognised her efforts for democratic rights and peaceful transition.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Backed González
strings.timeline.t3.text: Barred from running, she supported González; the opposition disputed official results.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Won opposition primary
strings.timeline.t4.text: Secured the main opposition alliance’s presidential nomination.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Lost parliamentary seat
strings.timeline.t5.text: Stripped of her seat during anti-government protests.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Entered National Assembly
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began parliamentary service after election in 2010.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-founded monitoring group
strings.timeline.t7.text: Helped establish Súmate to promote civic election monitoring.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Caracas
strings.timeline.t8.text: Grew up in Venezuela and later trained in industrial engineering.
